_note: THE NINE SILENT CUES THAT HAD NO EQUIVALENT IN THE LIBRARY (drop 0912k).
The other eleven silent cues were repointed at samples that already existed under another
name - that is the cheap half. These nine had nothing to borrow: there is no creature roar,
no mech footfall, no teleport in 164 files. They are the boss-presence cues, and their absence
is why the Magma Colossus, the Olive Warden and the Toxic Portal Warden move and attack without
Classes are declared per cue, after the first alert pass taught that a klaxon is dark by nature
and a rise is supposed to rise. A roar is a swell; a footfall and a clank are impacts.

sounds.prompt: A colossal armoured war machine bellowing. A deep grinding metallic roar with a distorted mechanical growl inside it, huge and slow, rising then falling. Menacing and heavy. Dry, no music, no long reverb tail. Retro arcade video game boss roar.

A giant machine screaming as it is destroyed. A tearing metallic shriek with servo whine and collapsing structural groans underneath, agonised and mechanical, falling in pitch as it dies. Dry, no music. Retro arcade video game boss death cry.

An enormous organic creature roaring from deep in its chest. A wet guttural bellow with a rasping edge, monstrous and alive, swelling and then cutting off. Dry, no music, no reverb tail. Retro arcade video game monster roar.
A huge creature shrieking in pain as it dies. A high tearing organic screech breaking into a wet gurgling collapse, falling away. Dry, no music. Retro arcade video game monster death.
A single heavy metal CLANK, a thick steel plate struck once, bright and ringing on the attack with a short metallic tail. Immediate. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game metal hit.

A giant mech taking one step. A heavy hydraulic servo whir then a solid weighty thud as the foot lands, with a small metallic rattle. The thud is the loudest part. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game mech footstep.
A sharp hissing spit of acid launched under pressure. A bright wet hiss with a spraying fizz, quick and venomous, gone fast. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game toxic attack.

Something materialising out of nowhere. A rising reversed synthetic shimmer that snaps into existence with a bright electric pop at the end. Clean and otherworldly. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game teleport in.

Something vanishing instantly. A bright electric snap immediately collapsing into a descending synthetic shimmer that shrinks away to nothing. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game teleport out.
